claim: Meta's Frontier AI Framework (Oct 2024) defines two risk categories — 'critical' and 'high' — for CBRN and cyber threats.

source.excerpt: Meta's Frontier AI Framework categorizes risks into 'critical' and 'high' levels for CBRN and cybersecurity threats. Mitigations escalate with risk level.

claim: Meta conducted red-teaming for Llama 4 in early 2025 focused on CBRN uplift, following the FAIF protocol.

source.excerpt: Llama 4 underwent CBRN-focused red-teaming in early 2025. No critical or high risk levels were crossed according to FAIF thresholds.

claim: Meta participated in the May 2025 Seoul AI Safety Summit and signed the Frontier AI Safety Commitments.

source.excerpt: Meta was among the 16 organizations signing the Frontier AI Safety Commitments at the Seoul AI Safety Summit (May 2025).

provenance.context: Seoul AI Safety Summit 2025 communique. URL: https://www.seoulaisummit.com/communique

claim: Meta did NOT submit a Winter 2025 FLI Index survey response.

source.excerpt: Meta did not submit a response to the FLI Winter 2025 industry survey.

provenance.context: FLI AI Safety Index Winter 2025 Appendix A. URL: https://futureoflife.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/AI-Safety-Index-Report_131225_Full_Report_Digital.pdf

claim: Meta's open-weights policy (July 2024) commits to releasing most frontier model weights publicly, with restricted release only for safety-critical models.

source.excerpt: Meta commits to releasing frontier model weights publicly. Restricted release is reserved for models with demonstrated catastrophic risk.
